I judged each item against the page 89 and 91 rows. The "Seen in Wellcare documents" note says outpatient hospital rows give $0 for skin biopsies and one copay for everything else. That note is not part of this plan's text.

The page 91 diagnostic row has three in-network lines:
- **Diagnostic mammogram:** $0 copay.
- **All other diagnostic radiology in "an outpatient setting":** $500 copay.
- **Other settings (physician office or freestanding facility):** $250 copay.

Items 0, 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 turn on which setting each line applies to:
- **Item 0:** "Outpatient setting" is read as the outpatient hospital, and the note supports one copay there. The $500 copay fits, so it is true.
- **Item 1:** The $250 line is for other settings (office or freestanding), not the outpatient hospital, so it is false.
- **Item 2:** Freestanding is named under the $250 line, so $500 is false.
- **Item 5:** The office is under the $250 line, so $250 is correct for the office. The item says office $250, which matches, so it is true. Item 6 says office $500, which is false.
- **Item 8:** Freestanding at $250 matches, so it is true.

Items 3, 4, 7 and 9:
- **Item 3:** Out-of-network diagnostic radiology is 20% coinsurance, which matches the page, so it is true. The benefit is `imaging.diagnostic`, which fits the row.
- **Item 4:** The $50 copay for X-rays is in network. The page shows it under the X-ray row, so it is true.
- **Item 7:** Out-of-network X-rays at 20% match the page, so it is true.
- **Item 9:** The $0 diagnostic mammogram copay matches, so it is true.

The in-network deductible also applies to the diagnostic row, but the item fields do not cover a deductible, so I did not mark any item false for it.
